subject: Post-call: FintechAI cost/pricing & latency trade-offs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechai.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T14:10:00Z
Subject: Post-call: FintechAI cost/pricing & latency trade-offs

Thanks for the call today — good to meet the FintechAI team. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

Call highlights / what you asked us to confirm:
- Monthly token volume (approx): you mentioned 8–15M generation tokens + 2–4M embedding tokens as a baseline, with growth to ~30–50M in 12 months.
- Traffic profile: bursty daytime QPS (~50–120 qps at peak), median response size ~350 tokens, median prompt size ~60 tokens.
- Latency SLO: you said p99 target is ~300ms for chat flows; some batch processing (summaries) can tolerate 1–2s.
- Budget: target range $5k–$12k/month initially; interested in unit economics target ~$350/1M tokens as a starting point.

High-level options we discussed (trade-offs):
1) Hosted (Standard): fastest time-to-value, no infra management. Best for onboarding and small pilots. Expect higher $/1M tokens but faster rollout and auto-scaling. Streaming reduces p99 latency for chat but adds ~10% cost at the same throughput.
2) Dedicated (Reserved capacity): lower unit cost at scale, predictable latency, better for stable high-volume workloads. Requires monthly commit (we'll draft options).
3) Hybrid: start on Hosted for the pilot, then move selected routes to Dedicated once patterns stabilize.

Specific knobs and their impact (rough guidance):
- Batching (larger max_batch): improves cost/tokens (up to ~25% savings) but increases median latency (40–100ms depending on qps).
- Streaming: reduces observed tail latency for interactive chat (you get tokens earlier), can increase cost due to reduced kernel efficiency (~5–15% depending on model).
- Quantization / model variant: 4-bit quantized variants reduce cost substantially but may impact output quality on some prompts — we can run A/B evals.

Requested next steps (my action items):
- I will send a detailed pricing breakdown (hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid) with per-route estimates and an initial SOW. See attached pricing sheet.
- Please confirm expected monthly token volumes (generation vs embeddings) and any hard latency SLOs per route (chat vs batch vs search).
- If feasible, schedule a 60–90 minute technical session with your infra/ML eng team next week to scope dedicated sizing.

Attachment: FintechAI_pricing_sheet_q3_v3.xlsx (pricing + model tier assumptions)

Thanks — talk soon.
\-- 
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechai.com>

Date: 2026-09-01T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: FintechAI cost/pricing & latency trade-offs

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. Quick answers and clarifications from our side: 

Usage/volume details (best current estimate):
- Active users: ~20k DAU (growth to 80k in 12 months).
- Typical session: 3–6 messages, average prompt 60 tokens, generated tokens ~350 per response.
- Expected monthly tokens (gen): ~12,000,000 (baseline), embeddings workload ~3,000,000 tokens/month. 12M could move to 30M+ in 6–12 months depending on rollout.

Latency SLOs:
- Chat (primary product): p99 target ~300ms. If we can get p95 ~200ms and p99 ~300ms that's ideal.
- Background batch jobs (weekly reports): can be 1–2s.

Budget:
- Initial budget slice for pilot: $5k–$8k/mo. If numbers look good for unit economics, we can commit more (up to $12k/mo) and discuss reserved capacity.

Question on streaming vs batching: our chat is interactive — users expect snappy token streaming. Does Redwood recommend streaming for chat where p99 target is 300ms? Any examples of cost delta vs batching for interactive flows?

Procurement timeline: aim to complete procurement and legal in 4–6 weeks if the pilot goes well.

Thanks — happy to take the pricing breakdown and the SOW. Would also like to loop in our infra lead for the technical deep-dive next week.

Best,
Alex

alex.turner@fintechai.com | +1 617 555 0112

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: FintechAI cost/pricing & latency trade-offs

Alex — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. Below is a more concrete breakdown and recommended path given your volumes and p99 target. 

High-level unit economics (estimates) — per 1M generation tokens (approx):
- Hosted (Standard tier, non-quantized models): ~$450 / 1M tokens — p95 ~250–500ms, p99 depends on burst profile. Streaming enabled reduces observed p99 but adds ~8–12% cost at similar throughput.
- Hosted (Opt-in batching/optimized kernels): ~$360 / 1M tokens (if routes can tolerate slightly higher median latency and batching), p95 increases ~60–120ms versus pure streaming.
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs, 1–3 month commit tiers): ~$220–$280 / 1M tokens depending on commit level and model variant — p95 ~150–300ms, much more predictable tail latency.
- Embeddings: ~$180 / 1M tokens (hosted) and ~$100 / 1M tokens (dedicated) — embeddings are cheaper per token but still significant at scale.

How knobs affect your case: 
- For interactive chat (p99 300ms): streaming is recommended for perceived latency (users see tokens as they arrive). Expect a cost premium (~8–12%) vs fully batched generation.
- If you can accept slightly higher median latency and pack requests into batches (max_batch=16–32), you can get ~15–25% cost savings vs streaming. This is a classic latency vs cost trade-off.
- We commonly recommend a hybrid routing policy: chat routes on streaming-backed hosted instances initially (fastest time-to-value + easy rate-limits), then migrate high-volume, predictable routes to Dedicated with batching optimization.

SLO-driven pricing / discount structure we can offer: 
- Pilot (no commit): standard hosted pricing.
- 3-month pilot -> Dedicated pilot discount: if you commit to a 3-month minimum for a dedicated pool sized for your 12M baseline, we can offer a 15% discount on dedicated rate card for the pilot period.
- Annual reserved commit -> custom blended $/1M target: e.g., a 12-month $X commit targeting 30M tokens/month could reach $180–$240 / 1M tokens depending on model selection and quantization.

Example scenario (your numbers):
- Baseline 12M gen + 3M embed (~15M tokens): Hosted streaming estimate ~= $5,400 / month (gen + embed combined using hosted numbers above). That aligns with your pilot budget range.
- If you move to Dedicated with a modest commit and batching optimizations, that could fall to ~$3,300–$4,200 / month effective (depending on commit).

Next concrete steps I propose: 
1) I’ll produce a two-page PoC estimate for the pilot (hosted streaming configuration) and a parallel Dedicated sizing worksheet (attached).
2) Schedule 60–90m technical deep-dive (we’ll bring runtime/infra) to confirm qps shaping, batching tolerance, and auth/net requirements.
3) If you’re ready, we’ll spin a 2-week pilot and provide usage telemetry + cost/per-route estimates.

Attachments: proposed_pricing_breakdown.xlsx (detailed calc), FintechAI_SOW_v2.pdf (initial scope)

If you confirm the baseline 12M/3M split and that chat requires streaming, I’ll get the PoC estimate over today and propose time slots for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks,
Marissa
